# Beginnings

Starting a process, a workflow of thinking, about a controversial idea is time consuming and frustrating.  

There are a host of psychological obstacles to just get going.  

tip:  notice when you start to tune out of your work, when you go to your phone to "self medicate" on social media:  What were you just reading before that?  What did your mind do before you grabbed a distraction device?  Track those things because you might discover an edge for you in regards to intellectual work. 


So, when you start this work, begin with some acceptance that you'll encounter blockages, frustrations, dead ends. Brute forcing your way through will not typically lead to satisfaction.  


I'm not sure the best way to think about it, to be honest. I usually find mysefl working in spurts...I'll have a lot of motivation and emotion, will get through it, and then have to just stop.  

I think this is normal.  I think it's common.  

Tip: have a system to track your progress so that when you come back to this work (next week, month, whenever), you don't waste a lot of time getting caught up to speed. call out to niklas lumen


# Identifying the claim

Sometimes it's not obvious.  Sometimes claims are implicit.   And that means time spent getting the claim out is worthwhile.

As an example, consider the claim that new gun laws should not be allowed because laws won't stop gun violence. 

On the one hand, there is a clear claim about gun laws, but what is implicit might be more important:
